newsitem.title: CHINA: China says HK handover demonstrates its rise.
newsitem.headline: China says HK handover demonstrates its rise.

text.p: China said on Monday the handover of the British colony of Hong Kong to Chinese rule next week was demonstration that the rise of the world's most populous nation was an indisputable fact.

"From decline to prosperity, from humiliation to glory; these two eras, these two fates fully demonstrate that the rise of China is an indisputable fact," the People's Daily said in reference to what China views as the humiliating loss of Hong Kong.

Britain seized Hong Kong after defeating China in the 19th-century "opium wars", but agreed in 1984 to hand back Hong Kong to Beijing at midnight on June 30 after more than 150 years of colonial rule.
Many in China believe Hong Kong's return was a result of China's growing strength and stature on the international stage.
The People's Daily, mouthpiece of the ruling Communist Party, said a plan by President Jiang Zemin to attend handover ceremonies in Hong Kong showed Beijing cared about the territory's future.

"President Jiang's coming to Hong Kong demonstrates the importance the central government attaches to Hong Kong compatriots and the future of Hong Kong," it said. Jiang would be the first Chinese head of state to set foot in the territory.
"Hong Kong will also have a better tomorrow," the newspaper said. China has billed the handover as one of its greatest events this decade, if not this century.
